title: Federal Law No. 2 of 2019 concerning the use of ICT in health fields
status: official reference (summary, not full legal text)
summary: UAE healthcare ICT legal framework. Official UAE government guidance describes confidentiality, integrity, authorization and availability of health information, and lawful use of healthcare ICT. A competent legal reviewer must interpret exact duties and exceptions.

title: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021: Protection of Personal Data
status: official reference; applicability must be checked
summary: General federal personal data protection framework. It has exclusions and special-sector arrangements, including treatment of government and regulated healthcare data; do not assume it directly governs every government healthcare processing activity. Refer applicability to qualified counsel alongside healthcare-specific law.
scope: UAE general data protection; qualified applicability check

title: UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031
summary: National AI strategy promoting smart government, AI integration, responsible governance, data capabilities, innovation and healthcare applications. Strategy supports institutional direction but is not a legal authorization to access sensitive data.

title: UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence (2024)
summary: Publicly published UAE charter addressing responsible development and use of AI. Use for human-centered oversight, trust and transparency concepts; precise institutional requirements require review of the source.

title: Cabinet Resolution No. 32 of 2020: Executive Regulation of health ICT law
status: official reference (summary, not full legal text)
summary: Executive regulation accompanying Federal Law No. 2 of 2019 on health ICT. Specific operational safeguards and applicability require reading the official regulation and obtaining institutional legal review.

title: ITU-T Y.3172: Architectural framework for machine learning in future networks
summary: ITU-T architecture for ML in future networks, including source, collector, preprocessor, model, policy, distributor and sink logical nodes, and orchestration. Used here by analogy for healthcare-government decision support, not as a claim of sector-specific certification.

title: ITU AI Ready: Analysis Towards a Standardized Readiness Framework
summary: AI readiness considers data governance, quality, interoperability, infrastructure, skills, AI use and contextualization, accountability and operational capabilities. Adapted to assessment questions for healthcare public services.

title: WHO Ethics and Governance of Artificial Intelligence for Health
summary: WHO guidance emphasizes human autonomy, safety, transparency, accountability, equity and sustainable AI for health. Non-binding international comparator, not UAE law.
